title: Shadow Traffic: global kill switch + per-route disable controls (no-deploy toggle)
creator: Sean Gallagher
content:
Goal
Add an operationally-safe kill switch for Shadow Traffic that can be toggled without deploy, plus per-route disable controls, with explicit semantics and auditability. This is a hard requirement for beta/GA given that shadow execution is non-critical but can create capacity and/or SLO risk if misconfigured.

Background / Why
Shadow Traffic executes mirrored requests asynchronously and must never affect the primary response. However, it can still:
- consume GPU capacity (queue backlog -> increased utilization)
- inflate telemetry volume / cardinality
- create incident risk from config mistakes (sampling too high, targets too expensive)

We need:
1) a GLOBAL kill switch to stop all shadow execution across regions quickly
2) a per-route disable to surgically stop shadowing on a route while leaving other routes running
3) a clear operational contract: what is stopped (execution), what continues (primary), what is still emitted (minimal counters)

Scope
In-scope:
- Global kill switch enforced in data plane prior to enqueue/execute
- Per-route disable control enforced in policy evaluation (control plane) + enforced in data plane as well (defense-in-depth)
- No-deploy toggles via: (a) admin config store + (b) Console Admin UI endpoint wiring
- Audit log entry on any toggle change (who/when/what)
- Metrics for verification (drop counts, kill switch state, last updated timestamp)
- Safe default behavior: if control-plane config is unavailable/unreadable, shadow is OFF

Out of scope:
- Pausing judge scoring only (we can add later as separate switch; for now kill switch stops the entire shadow pipeline)
- Complex allowlist-only toggles (customer allowlist remains in policy schema work in ENG-2420)

Functional requirements
A) Global kill switch
- Name: shadow_traffic.global_enabled
- Default: false in all environments until beta is enabled; once enabled, can be toggled to false at any time
- Propagation: <= 60 seconds to all regions (target), with eventual consistency acceptable
- Enforcement point: data plane (shadow runner enqueue path) MUST check this prior to enqueue. If false, do not enqueue.
- Failure mode: if config fetch fails OR value missing => treat as disabled

B) Per-route disable
- Name: shadow_traffic.route_enabled (route-level boolean, default false unless explicitly configured)
- Expressed as part of RoutePolicy evaluation result (policy engine) AND additionally checked by shadow runner using the computed policy snapshot included with the primary request metadata.
- If global is true but route is false => do not enqueue.

C) Admin toggles / no-deploy
- Provide an internal admin endpoint (authenticated) to set/get global kill switch state
- Provide an internal admin endpoint to set/get per-route override state (route_id/route_name)
- Wire endpoints behind Console Admin controls (feature-flagged for internal staff only)
- Log changes to audit log: actor, source IP (if available), old/new value, target (global/route), reason (freeform required)

D) Observability
- Emit counters:
  - shadow_eval.drop_total{reason="global_disabled"}
  - shadow_eval.drop_total{reason="route_disabled"}
  - shadow_eval.drop_total{reason="config_unavailable"}
- Emit gauge:
  - shadow_eval.kill_switch_global_enabled (0/1)
  - shadow_eval.kill_switch_last_update_ts (unix ts as label-less value; if our metrics stack can’t support, include in logs)
- Ensure tags follow cardinality guidance (no route_id in the global gauge; route_id only in drop counters if allowed by metrics tagging standard; if not allowed, aggregate at service level and rely on logs + join tables).

E) Security
- Endpoints must require elevated admin role (internal only). No customer-facing API in beta.
- All changes audited.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SRE can disable ALL shadowing within 60s without deploy.
- [ ] SRE can disable shadowing for a single route without impacting other routes.
- [ ] When disabled, primary requests behave identically (no extra latency on critical path beyond existing instrumentation), and no shadow jobs are enqueued.
- [ ] Verification procedure exists: dashboards/queries show drop_total increasing with correct reason.
- [ ] Config fetch failure results in shadowing being disabled (fail closed).
- [ ] Audit log entries exist for every change.

Implementation notes / Proposed approach
- Store kill switch state in existing “global dynamic config” store (same mechanism as rate-limit toggles) rather than relying on code flags.
- Shadow runner reads global config on a short TTL (e.g., 10–30s) with jitter. Route-level overrides come via policy snapshot (primary request metadata) but also have an override store path for emergencies.
- For per-route override store, key by canonical route_id (not route name) to avoid renames breaking the control.
- Data plane check order:
  1) global_enabled?
  2) route_enabled?
  3) capacity budget / backpressure checks
  => only then enqueue shadow job.

Rollout plan
- Land behind internal feature flag in staging.
- Exercise toggles during load test (ENG-2440) and confirm drop_total counters + no enqueue.
- Enable in prod with global default OFF.
- During beta: global ON only for allowlisted accounts/routes; keep ability to hard-disable globally within 1 minute.

Links / related work
- Linear: ENG-2419 (shadow runner execution path), ENG-2420 (RoutePolicy schema), ENG-2440 (SRE capacity/alerts)
- GitHub: PR-48302 (kill switch + admin override endpoints; Console admin integration)

Updates / comments
2025-10-28 (Sean Gallagher)
Created after SRE review: kill switch is a GA gate. Must be fail-closed and not rely on deploy. Adding explicit audit + drop reasons.

2025-11-01 (Benji Okafor)
Drafted API surface for internal admin endpoints. Confirmed we can reuse dynamic config store. Need to confirm route_id canonicalization with Policy Engine (Jordan).

2025-11-04 (Jordan Lee)
Policy engine can include route_id in the evaluated policy snapshot; recommend override store uses route_id, and runner does a strict match.

2025-11-07 (Rafael Mendes)
Request: add explicit drop_total reason=global_disabled and reason=route_disabled so oncall can verify within 1-2 mins. Also want last update timestamp visible somewhere.

2025-11-10 (Benji Okafor)
Implemented fail-closed behavior: if config read fails, treat as disabled and increment drop_total{reason=config_unavailable}. Added audit log hook requiring “reason” string.

2025-11-13 (Chloe Martin)
Console admin wiring ready behind internal flag. Confirmed permissions check: only internal admins group.

2025-11-18 (Sean Gallagher)
Verified in prod during shadow beta rehearsal: toggling global to OFF stops enqueue within ~20–30s; dashboard shows drop_total increasing with global_disabled. Marking done.
